Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the asks we captured so we can scope a technical qualification:  

Summary of current needs:

3) We will follow up with a short note on multi-region routing options (regional serving vs edge routing) and implications for data residency and fallback behavior.

Attachments: finova-slo-requirements.xlsx, regional-routing-diagram.png

If this looks right, please confirm the latency/throughput numbers and availability for next-week SE deep-dive.

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming our initial targets and a few clarifications below. I've attached our internal SLO doc for reference.

Confirmed targets (initial):
- Latency (p95): US: <150ms, EU: <150ms, APAC: <200ms
- Latency (p99): US/EU: <300ms, APAC: <400ms
- Sustained throughput: ~200 RPS across the fleet during peak; typical baseline ~50 RPS
- Burst: short spikes to ~600 RPS for up to 90s during batch job spikes
- Concurrency: average concurrent requests ~20, but we have a small set of power users that can reach ~50 concurrently
- Streaming: yes — we need token-level streaming for our new chat UI to start showing partial answers quickly
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain at rest in EU region (customer metadata + logs). APAC customers prefer APAC residency but can accept cross-border in rollouts if we have clear controls.

Attached: finova-slo-requirements.xlsx (filled), finova_internal_slo_notes.pdf

Availability for SE deep-dive: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–11:00 PDT / 13:00–14:00 EDT works for our team.

Thanks,
Sara Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
sara.chen@finova.com

Subject: Re: Finova - Performance SLOs & Multi-region Routing (follow-up)

Nice summary, Marissa — copied my quick technical read below so we can align before the SE deep-dive.

Quick assessment (preliminary):
- Targets look achievable with a combination of regional pinned model servers (US/EU/APAC) plus regional edge routing for lower latency on warm sessions.
- Streaming requirement is supported; we'll want to validate model size and token emission rates in the SE call. Streaming can increase concurrency/throughput demands since connections stay open longer — we should size for sustained 200 RPS with spikes to 600 RPS and concurrent connections up to 60 to be safe.
- Data residency: we can keep at-rest data and logs in-region for EU via private S3 buckets or customer-managed encryption keys (we'll document options). Audit logs can be routed to EU KMS/HSM.
- Fallback behavior: propose primary-region serving with automatic fallback to nearest region if capacity constrained; for EU-residency customers we can restrict cross-region fallback (policy-based).

Action items for SE deep-dive:
1) I will bring a sample load test config and latency profiles for the models we recommend.
2) Need Finova to share: sample requests per second CSV and a couple of representative payload sizes (avg/max tokens).
3) We'll prepare a short doc outlining routing options + cost/latency trade-offs.

Proposed meeting time confirmed: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00 PDT. I'll schedule a 45-minute session and include a shared Drive link with pre-reads.

Thanks,
Aditya
